name: rust_net_cudagraph_spike_20260803
what: Go/no-go spike: reach CUDA-Graph-class batch-1/batch-8 latency from Rust via ort IOBinding with device-resident tensors, per docs/RUST_NET_EVAL_DESIGN_20260802.md 6.2/7.1.
verdict: STOP (qualified). Graph capture REACHED from Rust and within ~4% of the torch reference; T1 faithfulness unchanged. Rejected because a quiet-box re-measurement of the DENOMINATOR moved it 1.55x (0.0903 -> 0.0584 ms/sim), putting cost_ratio at ~3.06 against a recorded break-even of ~2.4-2.6.

box.state: census-clean for the denominator and the section-4 numerator table; a CPU-side job from another session was live for raw_readout_gpu.txt (GPU idle throughout, loadavg stamped in that file's header)

stack.linking: ORT_LIB_LOCATION + ORT_PREFER_DYNAMIC_LINK=1; download-binaries deliberately NOT enabled (its build is CUDA-13 and fails OPEN to the CPU)

net.note: same ONNX exports and position dump as the memo; not checked in (~90 MB / ~258 MB)

denominator_ms_per_sim.adopted_rationale: mean of the 8-concurrent rows: the champion deploys parallel_workers=8 (CL-071), so the honest denominator is what ONE world sees while EIGHT run. It is only +2% over single-threaded, which also shows the Rust search is not DRAM-bandwidth-saturated at k=8.
denominator_ms_per_sim.memo_delta: the memo's denominator is 1.55x the quiet-box figure; its session had a live 13-worker eval throughout. No carc-core commit explains it (the memo was measured AT 3416f87, the perf-pass merge itself).

numerator_ms_forward_min.note: census-clean window, ORT default CUDA-EP knobs, min over 200-1000 reps

decision.bar_literal_result: PASS (0.176 even with the unoptimized synchronous upload folded in)
decision.governing_reading: substantive — the ms figure was a proxy for the break-even, and the proxy broke when the denominator moved
decision.only_passing_config: batch 64 (r 1.83, cost_ratio 2.29) — unreachable at k=8; needs cross-move or cross-game batching

acceptance_tiers.T0: unchanged (same artifacts, written under export_onnx.py's bit-identity assertion)

T1.note: all three identical in every reported digit incl. bit-exact count 179 — the device-resident, graph-captured path adds ZERO drift

acceptance_tiers.T3: PASS — .error_on_failure() plus runtime assertions that bound inputs AND the bound output landed on AllocationDevice::CUDA

traps_found.effect: FASTER (~3% at batch 8) AND WRONG — argmax 100.00% -> ~30%, max-abs 4.9e-4 -> 1.0, silently, on all three CUDA backends
traps_found.disposition: left wired up, DEFAULT OFF (matches ORT's default)

reopen_bar: a device reaching batch-8 per-leaf <= ~0.11 ms (r <= 2.0 at the MEASURED denominator), OR a batching design putting >=64 leaves in flight (pondering / cross-game) — a separate lever with its own gate
